solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not suitable for all hours, West Country follows the start of Easy Rider

indicators.note: follows places the West Country part after the opening letters already built
Not tells us to drop the letter for suitable from the word for all hours

parts.note: all hours is simply HOURS
U is the film certificate for a film suitable for everyone

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, here taken from Easy

parts.note: Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A complaint that a cult biker film is unsuitable for showing at any time of day, with West Country trivia attached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes U (suitable) from HOURS to leave HORS. 'Easy Rider' looks like the film title, but Easy gives only its E and Rider is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A female equestrian is a rider of horses.

clue.text: Perhaps proverbial rib, if somehow removed, could give some common ground

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of proverbial get rearranged once the other word's letters are taken away

parts.note: these three letters are the ones removed from the fodder

explanation.surface: A proverbial rib, if removed, might be the shared ground between two ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: take R, I and B out of PROVERBIAL ('removed') and the remaining PROVEAL rearranges ('somehow') to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Where two areas coincide they share some territory, an area of coincidence.

clue.text: Cutting s-strings?

parts.note: a harp is a stringed instrument, so it can stand for strings

explanation.surface: A stammered question about severed strings.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer gives a lone letter S, which goes before HARP (strings).
explanation.definitionFit: A keen blade is cutting, with a fine edge.

clue.text: Married woman gets quiet instead of loud? Pronounced scepticism to be eliminated

indicators.note: instead of says one letter takes another's place inside the married woman

parts.note: a married woman is a wife
f (forte) is the musical marking for loud
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: Pronounced asks for how the word for scepticism sounds when said, with its silent letter dropped

parts.note: scepticism is doubt

explanation.surface: A wife is told to tone down her voice while her husband's doubts are voiced and dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instead of' swaps F (loud) in WIFE for P (quiet), giving WIPE. DOUBT spoken has a silent B, so it sounds like DOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wiped out has been destroyed completely, eradicated.

clue.text: On demand, spins out lines said to be polite

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of on demand and spins are put out of order
said tells us to take the sound of the word for lines rather than its spelling

parts.note: cues are the lines that prompt an actor

explanation.surface: Someone told to spin records on request is reminded to stay courteous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges ONDEMANDSPINS into MINDONESPSAND. CUES (lines) 'said' is QS.
explanation.definitionFit: Watching your manners, especially in speech, is an idiom for courteous behaviour.

clue.text: To begin with, Calvin Klein made very little money

indicators.note: made suggests the letters are made into something new, reworked into another order
To begin with takes only the opening letter of Calvin

explanation.surface: Fashion designer Calvin Klein supposedly earned hardly anything at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To begin with' gives C from Calvin; 'made' rearranges C plus KLEIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The US five-cent coin is a small sum of cash.

clue.text: What may soothe and numb could become manoeuvrable

indicators.note: could become tells us the letters of manoeuvrable, once those of numb are taken out, turn into a new word

parts.note: these four letters are the ones that go with the answer to make up the fodder

explanation.surface: Something soothing and numbing might make a stiff joint easier to move.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: MANOEUVRABLE holds the letters of NUMB plus the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The succulent plant's gel is a well-known balm for burns and skin irritation.

clue.text: It's the end of the line for every coin

definitions.text: It's the end of the line

parts.note: every means all
coins are loose change

explanation.surface: A complaint that every coin has reached its terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the guard's call at a terminus telling passengers to leave the train.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway announcement at the terminus that everyone must get off the train.

clue.text: After dad nods off, send out for scraps

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of dad and nods go off into a new arrangement
out signals the letters of send are put out of order

explanation.surface: Once Dad has nodded off, someone is sent out to fetch leftovers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns DADNODS into ODDSAND; 'out' turns SEND into ENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscellaneous leftovers and bits are an idiomatic phrase for scraps.

clue.text: See 7 across
An iPad application includes a non-alcoholic drink and an alcoholic one

indicators.note: includes puts the soft drink inside the rearranged letters
application, the work of applying oneself, suggests the letters of an iPad are worked into a new order

parts.note: cola is a soft drink

explanation.surface: A tablet app is said to offer one soft drink and one cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'application' rearranges ANIPAD into PINADA, and 'includes' sets COLA inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The rum, pineapple and coconut cocktail is an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Went off to develop educational module

indicators.note: module, a component or part, says the answer is a part of the words develop educational

explanation.surface: Someone left to create a teaching unit.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'develop educational'.
explanation.definitionFit: To run off secretly, usually to marry, is to leave.

clue.text: Where skua finally hovered, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged another way
finally takes only the closing letter of skua

explanation.surface: A seabird hangs in the air above someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes A from skua, and 'perhaps' rearranges A plus HOVERED. The whole clue also describes where a hovering bird would be.
explanation.definitionFit: A hovering bird is above, up in the sky.

clue.text: Extremely powerful in a break to get appreciation

indicators.note: in places those letters within a and the word for break

parts.note: a pause is a break

indicators.note: Extremely takes the extreme letters, the first and last, of powerful

explanation.surface: A powerful performance in an interval wins praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives PL, the first and last letters of powerful, which go 'in' A PAUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping is how an audience shows it values a performance.

clue.text: Somehow makes inside toilets appear untidy

indicators.note: inside puts the rearranged letters within the word for toilets

parts.note: loos are toilets in British usage

indicators.note: Somehow suggests the letters of makes are rearranged in some fashion

explanation.surface: Somehow the toilets end up looking messy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges the letters of makes, and 'inside' puts them within the toilets; loo is everyday British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dishevelled or disordered in appearance is an idiom for being untidy.

clue.text: Underuse exposed

annotationWithheld.why: Underuse exposed (4): the blog reads UNDE as fodder and RUSE as the anagram indicator, both taken from the one printed word 'Underuse', so a single word does two jobs.

clue.text: City of Monte Carlo, except for the outskirts, is to be rebuilt

indicators.note: to be rebuilt says the letters are reassembled in a new order
except for the outskirts keeps only the inner letters of Carlo, dropping its first and last

explanation.surface: A whole city is to be rebuilt apart from the fringes of Monte Carlo.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping C and O from Carlo leaves ARL; 'to be rebuilt' rearranges MONTE plus ARL.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest city in Quebec, Canada.

clue.text: See 26
Trapped in marriage, court with excessive charm and affectation

indicators.note: Trapped in puts the court abbreviation inside the word for marriage

parts.note: a marriage is a union

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a marriage woos another with oily charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trapped in' sets the court abbreviation within the marriage word; the definition uses unction's figurative sense of oily, insincere earnestness.
explanation.definitionFit: Oily, affected earnestness or flattery, a sense taken from anointing with oil.

clue.text: Goes on making profit

definitions.meaning: to go on is to continue
profit is money taken from a sale

explanation.definitionFit: Proceeds means continues, as a verb; as a noun it means the money made from a sale.

clue.text: See 24
Magician is to speak in upcoming raffle

indicators.note: in puts the spoken word inside the reversed raffle
upcoming in a down clue means the word for raffle is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a raffle is a draw

indicators.note: to speak asks for how the word is sounds when said aloud, with a Z sound

parts.note: is is said with a buzzing final sound

explanation.surface: A conjuror is due to talk at a forthcoming prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: DRAW read 'upcoming' gives WARD; 'is', spoken, sounds like IZ, which goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wizard is a sorcerer who practises magic.

clue.text: Heard father, 23, is a pain

indicators.note: Heard asks for the sound of the words for father and the 23 answer said together

parts.note: father is sire, and 23 is the answer to 23 across, a slang word for the heart

explanation.surface: Someone hearing that father's heart is the problem.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent, 'sire' plus the 23-across answer sounds like 'sigh-a tick-a'. 'Heard' signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve pain running down the back of the leg is a painful condition.

clue.text: Heart timer

definitions.meaning: slang for the organ that beats in the chest
a clock or watch that measures time

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the heart, which beats; also a clock or watch, which keeps time.

clue.text: TV's snappy furniture

parts.note: snappy, irritable, means cross
a dresser is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A grumpy sideboard seen on television.
explanation.walkthrough: TV is short for transvestite, not television; 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A transvestite is someone who wears clothes of the opposite sex.

clue.text: Teams mix up with mounting style

parts.note: teams are sides
to addle is to muddle or mix up

explanation.surface: Teams are muddled about how to get on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A way of riding with both legs on one side of the horse, a riding position.

clue.text: Loves welcoming copper superintendent back for some Italian food

indicators.note: welcoming puts the reversed run inside the two letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O, so loves gives two of them

indicators.note: back says the copper and superintendent run is read backwards

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a superintendent is a boss

explanation.surface: Lovers take in a police superintendent returning for an Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the copper-plus-boss run round as one piece, and 'welcoming' lets the two tennis zeros enclose it.
explanation.definitionFit: Milanese braised veal shanks are an Italian dish.

clue.text: See 8
Showing a bit of leg in dance certain to be revealing

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word for dance

parts.note: a disco is a dance

indicators.note: a bit of leg is its opening letter

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: Showing a little leg at a disco is sure to reveal plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showing' looks like the definition but is only scene-setting; 'a bit of' takes the first letter of leg, which goes 'in' the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something known is an act of exposure or showing.
